The glb references the textures by relative URI (../../materials/<ch>/... and ../../materials/shared/...), it does not embed them: Godot resolves them to the res:// library PNGs on import and through runtime GLTFDocument (both tested). baseColorFactor is a palette tint over the library albedo, metallicFactor is set per zone, emissive textures are masks (EMISSION_OP_MULTIPLY). UV0 is world-scale box projection (1 UV unit = 1 m) except fitted module faces. Per v1.9, keep emission enabled on every loader-built surface (black when unlit). entries.source: Scripted Blender 5.2.3 (bpy) procedural modelling by the 3d-kits stream; source: assets/destructibles/source/blender/ (runchar.py, tfjenv.py)
entries.notes: Premium pass 2 (2026-11-10, SV-01, after review): smooth stylised forms instead of box primitives. Superellipse-lofted torso, bulged 12-sided limbs with ball joints, and every armour plate is a curved shell sampled from the body surface it sits on (chest, side, back, abdomen bands, pauldrons in two layers, bracers, thigh, knee, shin and toe guards) with a chamfered rim, so the suit reads as layered panels. Soft cloth hood (deep opening, soft brow point, loose folds, rolled rim) over a glossy black visor with cyan slits; cowl and V scarf; cross straps over the plates; belt pouches. Suit panel seams and cloth creases are baked into the normal map (bake-time bump). A shorter flowing cloth cape (12 x 10 grid, folds and a pointed hem, flaring back) is skinned to cape_rig (Skeleton3D on import, bones cape_root and a 3 x 3 grid cape_<column>_<row>) parented under torso, with sway keyed in every clip. Everything else is a rigid node rig, unchanged: hips > torso > head > hood, torso > arm_weapon > forearm_weapon > weapon_socket, torso > arm_support > forearm_support, hips > leg_r/leg_l > shin_r/shin_l. arm_weapon pivots at the right (camera-side) shoulder; rotation 0 aims along +X and the aim angle is a rotation about +Z, as in OperativeRig. Mount the weapon glb on weapon_socket with no offset (weapon origin = grip). The support arm is separate; copy a share of the arm_weapon rotation to arm_support if the far hand should follow the aim. Head carries the emissive visor slits (in the baked emission mask). Animations are node TRS clips at 30 fps, in place, every node keyed in every clip so clips can be switched cleanly. Material: one baked 1024 set embedded in the glb (chr_operative_a: albedo, tangent normal, ORM, emission mask; library surfaces from the surfaces stream baked through a unique UV), no COLOR_0. Per v1.9 keep emission enabled. Quality: stylised production candidate built procedurally; it reads well at game distance but is not a sculpted hero character (procedural shells, no cloth simulation, 5892 of 6,000 tris). Form language follows the project concept frames SV-01 to SV-07 (see their manifest entries); no concept pixels are used in the mesh. glb 4083 KB.

entries.notes: Nodes: mesh_intact (412 tris), mesh_light (412), mesh_heavy (744); show one at a time (all three import visible: hide mesh_light and mesh_heavy on instancing). Marker empties: fx_spark_01, fx_spark_02, fx_spark_03, fx_smoke_01. Material slots: emit_blue_cvt, emit_red_cvt, mat_concrete_cvt, mat_concrete_cvt_frame, mat_concrete_cvt_panel, trim_burnt_cvt, trim_cable_cvt, trim_dark_cvt, trim_edge_cvt, trim_internal_cvt, trim_trim_cvt. Premium pass (2026-11-10): every slot is textured from the surfaces stream library. The glb references the textures by relative URI (../../materials/<ch>/... and ../../materials/shared/...), it does not embed them: Godot resolves them to the res:// library PNGs on import and through runtime GLTFDocument (both tested). baseColorFactor is a palette tint over the library albedo, metallicFactor is set per zone, emissive textures are masks (EMISSION_OP_MULTIPLY). COLOR_0 carries baked ambient occlusion only (valid since v1.7; multiply it with albedo). Slots: mat_<material>_<ch>[_<zone>] main and zone finishes, trim_edge_<ch> is the worn edge highlight on bevels, trim_module_<ch> uses fitted UVs (one rack unit per blade) with the electronic_module emission mask, trim_<zone>_<ch> paint, rubber, cable, internals, burnt metal; emit_ and glass_ as named. UV0 is world-scale box projection (1 UV unit = 1 m) except fitted module faces. Per v1.9, keep emission enabled on every loader-built surface (black when unlit). Heavy state switches some compute light to the warning colour and turns others off (malfunction read); fx_spark_* mark exposed internals for spark VFX. Destroyed state: see CVT-DEB-CIVIC_COLUMN-A. glb 148 KB.

entries.notes: Single node mesh_intact (1380 tris) under a root named after the file. Material slots: emit_blue_cvt, emit_red_cvt, glass_smoked_cvt, mat_concrete_cvt, mat_concrete_cvt_frame, trim_dark_cvt, trim_internal_cvt, trim_trim_cvt. Premium pass (2026-11-10): every slot is textured from the surfaces stream library. The glb references the textures by relative URI (../../materials/<ch>/... and ../../materials/shared/...), it does not embed them: Godot resolves them to the res:// library PNGs on import and through runtime GLTFDocument (both tested). baseColorFactor is a palette tint over the library albedo, metallicFactor is set per zone, emissive textures are masks (EMISSION_OP_MULTIPLY). COLOR_0 carries baked ambient occlusion only (valid since v1.7; multiply it with albedo). Slots: mat_<material>_<ch>[_<zone>] main and zone finishes, trim_edge_<ch> is the worn edge highlight on bevels, trim_module_<ch> uses fitted UVs (one rack unit per blade) with the electronic_module emission mask, trim_<zone>_<ch> paint, rubber, cable, internals, burnt metal; emit_ and glass_ as named. UV0 is world-scale box projection (1 UV unit = 1 m) except fitted module faces. Per v1.9, keep emission enabled on every loader-built surface (black when unlit). Background layers are pre-darkened in baseColorFactor so they sit 30-50% below gameplay pieces. Form language follows the project concept frames SV-01 to SV-07 (see their manifest entries); no concept pixels are used in the mesh. glb 129 KB.

entries.rights_status: original procedural work: scripted Blender (bpy) code written by the 3d-kits asset agent (AI-assisted authorship); no third-party meshes, textures or concept pixels; ownership not legally settled for AI-assisted work; not marked commercially cleared. Premium-pass textures come from the surfaces stream library in this repo (see assets/materials/PRODUCTION_NOTES.md for their rights note)
entries.used_by: MissionView near-back layer, z -2.5 .. -4 (props, no collision; never taller than 3 m behind a critical asset)
entries.pivot: bottom centre (x and z centred, lowest point at y = 0)
entries.dimensions: 1.6 x 1.35 x 0.8 m (w x h x d)
entries.notes: Single node mesh_intact (124 tris) under a root named after the file. Material slots: emit_cyan_mrd, emit_violet_mrd, mat_electronic_module_mrd, mat_electronic_module_mrd_panel, trim_dark_mrd. Premium pass (2026-11-10): every slot is textured from the surfaces stream library. The glb references the textures by relative URI (../../materials/<ch>/... and ../../materials/shared/...), it does not embed them: Godot resolves them to the res:// library PNGs on import and through runtime GLTFDocument (both tested). baseColorFactor is a palette tint over the library albedo, metallicFactor is set per zone, emissive textures are masks (EMISSION_OP_MULTIPLY). COLOR_0 carries baked ambient occlusion only (valid since v1.7; multiply it with albedo). Slots: mat_<material>_<ch>[_<zone>] main and zone finishes, trim_edge_<ch> is the worn edge highlight on bevels, trim_module_<ch> uses fitted UVs (one rack unit per blade) with the electronic_module emission mask, trim_<zone>_<ch> paint, rubber, cable, internals, burnt metal; emit_ and glass_ as named. UV0 is world-scale box projection (1 UV unit = 1 m) except fitted module faces. Per v1.9, keep emission enabled on every loader-built surface (black when unlit). Background layers are pre-darkened in baseColorFactor so they sit 30-50% below gameplay pieces. Form language follows the project concept frames SV-01 to SV-07 (see their manifest entries); no concept pixels are used in the mesh. glb 17 KB.
